message.content: {"summary":"Excellent work — you scored 39/40. The only gap is communication: a few answers (Q1, Q2, Q4) sit at or slightly above the 150-word limit, which cost one mark.","next_steps":["Trim Q1, Q2 and Q4 to comfortably under 150 words by cutting general textbook background and keeping only scenario-specific justification.","Practise drafting answers to a word budget: state the recommendation or choice first, then add only the two or three strongest scenario-linked reasons.","Keep your current habits — showing working, naming concrete techniques, and acknowledging downsides — as they are exactly what the top rubric levels reward."],"criteria":{"C1":"Excellent (6/6). Your modular monolith recommendation is supported by two scenario-specific trade-offs (five developers vs eight-plus services; load profile) and you explicitly acknowledge the downside of independent scaling. Maintain this pattern of naming the accepted cost of your recommendation.","C3":"Excellent (8/8). All three parts are correct with working shown: the series product 99.30%, 5.0 h downtime, and the parallel payment pair giving 99.80% and 1.5 h, all at the requested precision. Continue showing your intermediate products so your method stays verifiable.","C4":"Excellent (5/5). This full coverage is what the single-mark rubric requires.","C5":"Excellent (6/6). You justified AP for browsing and CP for payments, used the CAP theorem correctly, and named concrete techniques (Redis TTL cache; idempotency keys). Keep pairing each consistency/availability choice with a named mechanism to stay at this level.","C6":"Excellent (5/5). Your ADR has a scenario-specific Context, a clear Decision, and both positive and negative Consequences tied to CampusEats. This balance of consequences is exactly what distinguishes Excellent from Proficient — keep including at least one negative consequence.","C7":"Proficient (3/4). Your writing is clear, headings and IEEE citations are correct, but Q1, Q2 and Q4 sit at or slightly above the 150-word limit. To reach Excellent, trim each answer comfortably under the limit while keeping the scenario-specific justification."}}
